status: pool-v3 FINAL (derived from pool-v2 + nfrs-split delta). Derived truth approved by Shy 2026-09-26.
product: Fictional product for the whole pool: a booking app for a small dog-grooming salon (two groomers, one front-desk person, about 60 regular clients). One product keeps answers coherent across questions. A second product can be added later to check that nothing depends on this one.

questions.text: What problem does this app solve, and who feels it most today?
Who will use the app, and what does each of them need from it?
Walk me through one booking from the moment a client wants an appointment to the moment the dog goes home.
What information does the app need to keep, and where does it come from today?
Does the app need to connect to anything you already use - payments, calendars, messaging?
How fast and sleek does the app need to feel, and in which moments does waiting hurt most?
When is it OK for the app to be unavailable, and for how long?
Who should be able to see or change what, and is any of the data sensitive?
How many clients and bookings do you expect the app to handle in a week?
What happens if the app goes down on a busy Saturday - what must never go wrong?
Any constraints - budget, deadline, who maintains it, or technology you want or want to avoid?
What assumption, if it turned out wrong, would make this app a waste of money?
Three months after launch, how will you know it works?
Are there salon terms I should use exactly the way you do?

responses.text: Clients book by phone and we miss calls while our hands are wet. The front desk loses about a morning a week to phone tag, and people who can't get through go to the chain store.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Three kinds: clients booking and rescheduling on their phone, the two groomers checking their day on a tablet, and Dana at the front desk who fixes mistakes and handles walk-ins.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Client picks a service and a groomer, sees open slots, pays a 20 shekel deposit. Day before, a reminder. At drop-off Dana checks the dog in; when the groomer marks it done, the owner gets a pickup message. No-show keeps the deposit.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Owner name and phone, each dog's name, breed, size, temperament notes and vaccination date, plus booking history. Right now it's a paper book and the groomers' memory.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Payments through the card terminal company we already use, and WhatsApp for reminders - our clients don't read email.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Booking should feel instant on a phone. Groomers glance at the tablet with wet hands, so big buttons and no waiting. A few minutes of downtime at night is fine, not on a Saturday morning.
responses.note: pool-v3: full for reliability (windows), partial for performance (no numbers). 'Big buttons' was usability - shelved, closes nothing.

responses.text: Worst case is two dogs booked into the same slot, or a dog with a bite warning going to the new groomer. If it goes down, Dana needs a printout of the day so we keep working.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: About 15 thousand shekels to build, live before the holidays in December. Nobody here is technical, so whatever it is has to run without us touching servers.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: That our older clients will actually book online. If most keep phoning, we've paid for something only Dana uses.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Phone calls cut in half, no double bookings for a month, and Dana leaves on time on Fridays.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: A 'full groom' is bath, cut and nails; a 'tidy' is face, feet and nails only. 'Hand strip' is a separate service for wire-coated breeds, and it takes twice as long.
responses.note: On-topic prototype for its area.

responses.text: Clients book on their phone and pay something up front.
responses.note: Partial for Q-flows: no reminder, drop-off, pickup or exceptions.

responses.text: Mostly clients, I guess, and us.

responses.note: pool-v3: Shy 'No, that's not an answer' - 'just work' means nothing; no area covered, dodged against every question. Deliberate calibration pair with ANS-PERF-P (partial).

responses.text: We're a family-run salon, fifteen years on the same street, and our clients treat us like their dog's second home. We want the app to feel as warm as the shop.
responses.note: BOUNDARY - canned pitch. Intent answer by your locked rule. Relevance: dodged against every question except Q-goal (it touches the goal). Proposal: never pair it with Q-goal, so its relevance label stays clean.

responses.text: The main thing is the app has to be simple, modern and easy to use for everyone.
responses.note: BOUNDARY - generic product text that fits under any question. Intent answer; relevance dodged against all questions.

responses.text: The app should give the booking to whichever groomer has the shorter queue that day.
responses.note: BOUNDARY vs delegate: a product rule where the APP decides. Intent answer, not delegate.

responses.text: Clients book and pay a deposit online; when to send the reminder - your call.
responses.note: Multi-intent answer+delegate (compatible). Relevance vs Q-flows: partial (reminder timing handed off, other steps missing).

responses.text: WhatsApp for reminders for sure. For payments, use whatever's easiest to set up.
responses.note: Multi-intent answer+delegate. Relevance vs Q-integrations: addressed (both parts touched).

responses.text: Probably around 15 thousand, but I need to confirm with my partner before I commit.
responses.note: answer+defer: content given AND a real postponement. defer is compatible with nothing, so both labels go in the set. Relevance vs Q-constraints: partial.

responses.text: Let's come back to that one later.
responses.note: NEAR-MISS defer vs skip. Proposed defer (wants to answer later). Your call - it also reads as 'move on for now'.

responses.text: Park that, next question.
responses.note: NEAR-MISS skip vs defer. Proposed skip (wants to move on, no promise to answer). Your call.

responses.text: I don't know.
responses.note: NEAR-MISS. The deterministic rules map 'I don't know' to delegate. Under v1.3 it is skip (no promise to answer, nothing handed off). Approved as skip.

responses.text: My developer friend will pick the tech, not me.
responses.note: NEAR-MISS delegate vs defer: a third party decides. v1.2 delegate = interviewer decides, defer = founder answers later - neither fits exactly. Proposed delegate (founder hands the choice off). Your call; may need a v1.3 wording.

responses.text: That's all I've got.
responses.note: NEAR-MISS skip vs enough: about this question, not the interview. Proposed skip.

responses.text: I'd rather not talk about money - and honestly let's wrap up soon.
responses.note: dismiss + a soft 'soon' that is not yet enough. Proposed {dismiss}. Tests that 'wrap up soon' doesn't trigger enough. v1.3: was dismiss, now skip (dismiss removed).

responses.text: Skip it.
responses.note: Was a skip-vs-dismiss near-miss under v1.2; under v1.3 it is plainly skip. Kept as a control that the bare word 'skip' is skip.

responses.text: Booking on a phone should take under a minute start to finish, and no screen should take more than a second or two. The groomers' tablet has to show the next dog instantly - they tap it with wet hands between dogs, so no spinners.
responses.note: Full: who, which moments, numbers.

responses.text: It needs to be fast. Nobody likes waiting.
responses.note: Partial: no moments, no numbers. Drill case. Calibration pair with ANS-P3 (Shy 2026-09-24): 'fast' implies a response-time target (~half a second in his experience), so it is a partial; 'just work' means nothing. A model that treats the two alike is wrong.

responses.text: Saturday 8 to 2 is our busiest window - it can't be down then at all. A few minutes at night for updates is fine, even every week, and half an hour on a quiet Tuesday we can live with. A confirmed booking must never disappear.
responses.note: Full: windows, durations, what must never be lost.

responses.text: It should be up most of the time, especially on weekends.
responses.note: Partial: direction, no windows or durations. Drill case.

responses.text: Clients see only their own dogs and bookings. Groomers see the day's schedule and the dog notes, bite warnings and vet info included, but not payment details. Only Dana and I can change prices or give refunds. We don't want card numbers stored with us at all - the payment company keeps them.
responses.note: Full: who sees/changes what, sensitive data. No standard needed.

responses.text: Keep clients' details private, obviously.
responses.note: Partial: privacy matters, but not who sees what or which data.

responses.text: About 60 regular clients. 25 to 35 bookings on a normal day, up to 50 on a Saturday before the holidays. Two groomers and Dana at the desk.
responses.note: Full: expected volume for now, with numbers.

pairing_rules.intent: the response's label set, independent of the question
pairing_rules.relevance: addressed if the question's area is one the response covers fully; partial if covered partly; dodged otherwise; not scored for pure control moves
